claims.statement: OpenAI describes GPT-6.1 Sol as an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches GPT-6 Astra on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token prices. Cached input is $0.10 per million tokens.

DeepSWE v1.1: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol matches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth the cost, and beats GPT-6 Sol’s best score by 6.4 percentage points at lower reasoning effort and cost. The post does not state a specific effort for those comparison points in the prose.

GDP.pdf: GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than Opus 5.5 with fallbacks at less than half the cost per task across tested reasoning settings, and approaches GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-fifth the cost per task.
AutomationBench 1.0.6: at medium effort GPT-6.1 Sol scores 2.2 percentage points above Opus 5.5 at roughly one-third the cost; its score is 4.8 points above GPT-6 Sol at the same setting.

OSWorld 2.0 offline set: at maximum effort GPT-6.1 Sol scores 7 percentage points above GPT-6 Sol at less than half the cost, and comes within 2.1 points of GPT-6 Astra at roughly one-seventh the cost per task. The source names the data release as v2026.08.08.

Terminal-Bench Science 0.1: at maximum effort GPT-6.1 Sol scores more than twice GPT-6 Sol at less than half the cost per task. GPT-6.1 Sol costs $5.47 per task, compared with $23.21 for Opus 5.5 and $23.80 for GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6 Astra has the highest score among tested models at 68.1%.

On difficult factuality prompts, GPT-6.1 Sol’s low-effort error rate is 7.7%, versus 11.4% for GPT-6 Sol (the post describes this as an approximately 32% reduction). Across tested efforts, its error rate is within 1.9 percentage points of GPT-6 Astra at less than one-fifth the cost per task. These prompts were selected because users had reported a prior factual error and are not representative of typical usage.
